data.name: Neptune: Arena FPS
data.detailed_description:
Welcome to Neptune: Arena FPS
Classic arena style gameplay mixed with modern and futuristic elements, where the only thing that matters is the skill.

Features:

  • Set into a futuristic environment, you will have to fight the other players climbing the leaderboard and becoming the best;
  • Fast paced, tricky, get quick into the action without having to wait for the matches to end;
  • Beautiful arenas where only the best players will be able to dominate;
  • Many jump pads! Melt your movement skills with in-air fights;
  • Traps! Every map has its own way to endanger the player;
  • Master 9 futuristic but classic arena style weapons;
  • Offline single player BOT Practice;
  • Classic Deathmatch and Instagib mode;

Weapons skins


Modern experience system

  • Gain XP when fragging the other players;
  • Earn new ranks and get Tokens to spend on weapons skins;
  • Customize your player’s skin colour;

Steam Trading Cards

reviews.review:
Neptune: Arena FPS, developed and published by GENOVA Softworks, is an unapologetic throwback to the golden age of competitive first-person shooters. Rather than chasing modern trends like hero abilities, seasonal content, or extensive progression trees, the game embraces a design philosophy rooted in speed, precision, and player mastery. From the moment players enter its futuristic battlefields, it becomes apparent that Neptune was created with longtime fans of arena shooters in mind. Its premise is refreshingly simple: arm yourself, stay in motion, and outplay your opponents through skill alone.

The game's biggest strength lies in its commitment to traditional arena FPS mechanics. Matches are built around quick movement, weapon control, and map awareness, demanding constant engagement from players. Every encounter feels immediate, with little room for hesitation. Neptune's featured modes, including classic Deathmatch and the ever-demanding Instagib mode, reinforce this philosophy by rewarding reflexes and accuracy over unlocks or stat advantages. In Deathmatch, success often comes down to understanding weapon placements and controlling key areas of the map, while Instagib offers a more unforgiving experience where a single shot can completely change the outcome of a match.

GENOVA Softworks also makes an effort to modernize the formula through its visual presentation. Neptune adopts a science-fiction aesthetic filled with metallic environments, glowing accents, and futuristic architecture that complement its high-speed gameplay. The maps are designed to encourage fluid traversal, featuring open spaces and vertical elements that allow players to maintain momentum throughout a match. Although the game's production values understandably fall short of larger studio releases, its visual identity remains cohesive and effective. The art direction succeeds in creating arenas that are easy to read during intense firefights, which is an important consideration for any competitive shooter.

Another notable aspect of Neptune is its accessibility. The game does not overwhelm players with complicated systems or unnecessary distractions. It delivers exactly what its title promises: arena-based FPS combat. This focused approach gives the experience a certain charm, especially for players who miss the straightforward multiplayer titles of previous decades. Steam integration features such as achievements, cloud support, and trading cards further enhance the package, adding a modest sense of progression outside the matches themselves. Single-player support also provides an alternative for those unable to find online opponents, though the core experience is undeniably designed around multiplayer competition.

That said, Neptune's greatest challenge is one shared by many independent multiplayer games: maintaining an active player base. Arena shooters thrive on healthy communities, and the lack of a consistently populated matchmaking environment can limit the game's long-term appeal. New players may also find its skill ceiling intimidating. Without modern onboarding systems or forgiving mechanics, Neptune expects players to learn through experience, which can be both rewarding and frustrating depending on one's familiarity with the genre. Those seeking a casual shooter experience may struggle with the game's uncompromising nature.

Despite these shortcomings, Neptune: Arena FPS remains an admirable project. It captures the essence of classic competitive shooters with sincerity and confidence, offering an experience that values talent and practice above all else. It may not revolutionize the genre, but it doesn't need to. Its purpose is to preserve a style of gameplay that has become increasingly uncommon, and in that regard, it succeeds. For players yearning for the fast-paced intensity of old-school arena combat wrapped in a futuristic package, Neptune provides a worthwhile return to familiar territory.

Rating: 6/10
